The Streaked gurnard, Chelidonichthys lastoviza, exhibits a life-history strategy typical of many temperate demersal fishes, with size and age at maturity strongly modulated by environmental temperature. In populations studied at a mean water temperature of 11.8 °C [T = 11.8 °C], females attain puberty at a total length of 19.5 cm [Lp = 19.5 cm], a size that corresponds to a wet weight of approximately 70.6 grams [Wwp = approximately 70.6 grams] based on length-weight relationships derived from regional surveys. This relatively modest size at the onset of gonadal development suggests that individuals begin investing in reproductive tissues after a substantial portion of somatic growth has already been completed, a pattern common among triglid fishes that face size-dependent predation risk on soft-bottom continental shelf habitats. At a water temperature of 11.8 °C [T = 11.8 °C], the gonadosomatic index (GSI) was 4% [GSI = 4%] during the pre-spawning period.

As development proceeds during the early life stages, the embryonic and larval phases of C. lastoviza are critically temperature-dependent. Under laboratory incubation at a constant 11.8 °C [T = 11.8 °C], the age at birth, defined as the moment of chorion rupture and emergence of the yolk-sac prolarva, is nine days [ab = nine days]. This abbreviated pre-hatching period is characteristic of fishes that release pelagic, positively buoyant eggs, where rapid development reduces the window of vulnerability to benthic egg predators. The newly emerged prolarvae possess a small residual yolk sac and commence endogenous feeding; their extremely low wet weight at birth, estimated at 0.00080 grams [Wwb = 0.00080 grams], reflects the tiny oocyte diameter typical of triglids and places the species among those with exceptionally high fecundity per spawning bout. Initial observations of the cleavage-stage embryo reveal a transparent chorion that permits continuous monitoring of morphogenesis until eclosion.

Following the onset of exogenous feeding, the pelagic larvae of the Streaked gurnard undergo a period of rapid growth and morphological differentiation before settling to a demersal existence. The ultimate total length that individuals of this species can achieve over their lifetime is 40 cm [Li = 40 cm], a maximum size that is consistent with values reported for other medium-bodied triglids inhabiting the northeastern Atlantic and Mediterranean Sea. This asymptotic length is reached through a growth trajectory that decelerates markedly after maturation, with females, which typically attain larger sizes than males, investing heavily in reproductive output. Correspondingly, the ultimate female wet weight derived from the length-weight power function is 623 grams [Wwi = 623 grams], a body mass that reflects the substantial somatic reserves necessary to sustain repeated spawning events over several seasons. Adult fish are benthic-oriented and use their free pectoral-fin rays to probe the substrate for crustacean prey, a feeding ecology that likely influences their seasonal patterns of energy storage and reproductive readiness.

The lifespan of C. lastoviza under natural conditions, when considered at the same thermal regime of 11.8 °C [T = 11.8 °C], extends to approximately 18 years, equivalent to 6570 days [am = 6570 days]. This longevity is relatively high for a fish of its body size and suggests a slow pace of life, with late maturity and repeated spawning events across multiple years. The extended lifespan likely buffers the population against years of poor recruitment, allowing older, more fecund females to contribute disproportionately to the larval pool during favorable environmental windows. Field mark-recapture studies have confirmed that individuals exceeding 30 cm in total length are common in unfished populations, validating the growth parameters estimated from otolith analyses.

Comparative analyses within the genus Chelidonichthys reveal that the size at first reproduction of the Streaked gurnard is notably smaller than that of its larger congener, the tub gurnard (Chelidonichthys lucerna). At 19.5 cm [Lp = 19.5 cm] total length, puberty in C. lastoviza occurs earlier in the growth trajectory, allowing individuals to initiate gametogenesis at a relatively modest body size. The corresponding wet weight at this pubertal stage, 70.6 grams [Wwp = 70.6 grams], represents less than 12 percent of the ultimate female mass of 623 grams [Wwi = 623 grams], indicating that the species allocates a comparatively small proportion of its lifetime growth to the pre-maturation period. From an ecological perspective, this early onset of reproductive maturity may be an adaptation to the variable recruitment success typical of temperate shelf environments, where the ability to reproduce multiple times across a long lifespan offsets the uncertainty of juvenile survival.
